summary: Iteration 8 — single-admin JWT auth layer. Backend: 33/33 pytest cases PASSED covering login (success + wrong pw + unknown email + case-insensitive), /auth/me (with/without/malformed/forged token, no Bearer), all 9 protected mutating endpoints returning 401 without token, forged-signature rejection, upload+resource create+delete with valid Bearer, all public GET endpoints still open, credits Sem1=22 / Sem2=22.5 regression. Frontend: /admin renders AdminLogin when unauth, wrong-password shows admin-login-error 'Invalid credentials', correct login shows Manage dashboard with admin-signed-in-as chip=yashadesh.13@gmail.com, token persisted in localStorage.bitverse_admin_token, reload keeps session, Sign Out clears token and returns to login, notes upload with Bearer token succeeds (TEST_iter8_frontend_upload appears in Uploaded list). Auth layer is production-ready.

issues: React hydration warning in browser console: '<span> cannot be a child of <option>' — comes from the dev overlay/instrumentation wrapping <option> children in a <span data-ve-dynamic>. Cosmetic only, does not affect functionality but pollutes console. Consider suppressing or restructuring option children.

critical_code_review_comments: server.py auth is clean — bcrypt password hash (starts with $2b$), idempotent seed_admin() rotates password if env changes, JWT HS256 with sub+role+exp+iat, require_admin checks role AND sub matches ADMIN_EMAIL. Good.

LoginBody has no rate-limit / brute-force lockout. For a public single-owner console this is a minor risk; consider a simple IP-based lockout after 5 fails if the site gets scraped. Not required for MVP.
JWT_SECRET is fine (64 hex chars, well above the 32-byte HMAC minimum).
Token is stored in localStorage (susceptible to XSS). For single-admin site it's acceptable; httpOnly cookie would be more secure but requires CORS-with-credentials + CSRF handling. Not a blocker.
Frontend AuthProvider correctly clears localStorage on 401 from /auth/me, so stale tokens self-heal. Good.
Admin.jsx is 618 lines with 9 sub-forms — consider splitting into /pages/admin/*.jsx modules for maintainability. Not blocking.
